::: {#pixel-size .ck-sec}

## Finding the right pixel size

Grid resolution is often chosen by habit (30 m because that's Landsat). Hengl (2006) set out rules that tie it to what the data can actually support. For each aspect of a dataset they give a **coarsest legible** resolution (the largest pixel that still represents it), a **finest legible** resolution (below which pixels "are probably just waste of memory") and a **recommended compromise**. Fill in whatever you know; the overall range is where the rules agree.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="px"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const NICE = [0.5, 1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10, 12.5, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 75, 90, 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 5000, 10000];
  HM.tool({
    id: 'px', step: 'Working scale', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { sn: 50000, r95: 15, area: 10, n: 100, lay: 'random', hr: 525 },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'sn', l: 'Scale number of the output map (e.g. 50000 for 1:50,000)', t: 'num' },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Positioning error (optional)' },
      { k: 'r95', l: '95% error radius (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 }, { k: 'r99', l: '99% error radius (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 }, { k: 'rbar', l: 'Average error (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Point samples (optional)' },
      { k: 'area', l: 'Area of the study (km²)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'n', l: 'Number of sampled points', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'lay', l: 'Sampling layout', t: 'seg', d: 'random', opts: [['random', 'Random or irregular'], ['grid', 'Regular']] },
      { k: 'xy', l: 'Coordinates in metres, x, y per line (gives the distances between closest point pairs)', t: 'textarea', rows: 3 },
      { k: 'hr', l: 'Range of spatial dependence (m)', t: 'num', h: 'The distance at which the variogram levels off (the practical range).' },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Objects and terrain (optional)' },
      { k: 'abar', l: 'Average size of delineations (m²)', t: 'num', w: 2 }, { k: 'amld', l: 'Smallest object to map (m²)', t: 'num', w: 2 }, { k: 'wmld', l: 'Narrowest object (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'cont', l: 'Total length of contours (km), with the area above', t: 'num' }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const rows = [], warn = [];
      const add = (rule, coarse, fine, rec, why) => rows.push({ rule, coarse, fine, rec, why });
      if (v.sn > 0) add('Working scale (1:' + HM.fmt(v.sn, 0) + ')', 0.0025 * v.sn, 0.0001 * v.sn, 0.0005 * v.sn, 'Coarsest ≤ 0.0025·SN (four cells in the 0.25 cm² minimum legible delineation); finest ≥ 0.0001·SN (0.1 mm location accuracy on the map); recommended = 0.0005·SN (the 0.5 mm rule).');
      if (v.r95 > 0 || v.r99 > 0 || v.rbar > 0) add('GPS positioning error', v.r99 > 0 ? 1.8 * v.r99 : null, v.rbar > 0 ? v.rbar * Math.sqrt(Math.PI) : null, v.r95 > 0 ? 1.8 * v.r95 : null, 'Coarsest ≤ 1.8·r(99%); finest ≥ average error·√π (the error circle fits in one pixel); recommended = 1.8·r(95%) (95% of fixes fall within the pixel).');
      if (v.abar > 0 || v.amld > 0 || v.wmld > 0) add('Size of reference objects', v.abar > 0 ? Math.sqrt(v.abar) / 4 : null, v.wmld > 0 ? v.wmld / 2 : null, v.amld > 0 ? Math.sqrt(v.amld) / 4 : null, 'Coarsest ≤ √(average delineation size) ÷ 4; finest ≥ narrowest width ÷ 2; recommended = √(smallest object) ÷ 4, as in Table 1. (The text\'s Eq. 7 gives the looser √(a/4), four pixels per object; Table 1\'s forms are used here. Table 1 prints the finest as √w ÷ 2; w ÷ 2 is used, as a width can\'t be square-rooted.)');
      const A = v.area > 0 ? v.area * 1e6 : null;
      let pts = String(v.xy || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.split(/[,;\t\s]+/).map(Number)).filter(q => q.length >= 2 && isFinite(q[0]) && isFinite(q[1]));
      if (pts.length < 3) pts = null;
      const N = pts ? pts.length : v.n;
      let hbar = null, h5 = null;
      if (pts) { const nnd = pts.map((p, i) => { let b = Infinity; pts.forEach((q, j) => { if (i !== j) { const d = Math.hypot(p[0] - q[0], p[1] - q[1]); if (d < b) b = d; } }); return b; }).sort((a, b) => a - b); hbar = nnd.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / nnd.length; h5 = nnd[Math.floor(0.05 * (nnd.length - 1))]; }
      if (A && N > 1) {
        const s = Math.sqrt(A / N);
        add(`Inspection density (${HM.fmt(N, 0)} points)`, 0.1 * s, 0.05 * s, 0.0791 * s, 'Coarsest ≤ 0.1·√(A/N); finest ≥ 0.05·√(A/N); recommended = 0.0791·√(A/N) (2.5 observations per cm² of map with the 0.5 mm rule).');
        const hb = hbar ?? (v.lay === 'grid' ? s : 0.5 * s);
        add('Distance between points', hb / 2, h5, (v.lay === 'grid' ? 0.5 : 0.25) * s, `Coarsest ≤ half the mean distance between closest point pairs (${hbar ? 'from your coordinates' : v.lay === 'grid' ? '√(A/N) on a regular grid' : '≈ 0.5·√(A/N) for random points'}); finest ≥ the 5% shortest closest-pair distance${h5 ? '' : ' (needs coordinates)'}; recommended = ${v.lay === 'grid' ? '0.5' : '0.25'}·√(A/N).`);
        if (v.hr > 0) {
          let m, how;
          if (pts) { m = 0; for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) for (let j = i + 1; j < pts.length; j++) if (Math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[j][0], pts[i][1] - pts[j][1]) <= v.hr) m++; how = 'counted from your coordinates'; }
          else { m = Math.min(N * (N - 1) / 2, N * (N - 1) / 2 * Math.PI * v.hr * v.hr / A); how = 'estimated for points spread over the area'; }
          add('Spatial dependence structure', v.hr / 2, h5, m >= 1 ? v.hr * Math.pow(m, -1 / 3) : null, `Coarsest ≤ range ÷ 2; finest ≥ the 5% shortest closest-pair distance${h5 ? '' : ' (needs coordinates)'}; recommended = range × m^(−1/3), with m = ${HM.fmt(m, 0)} point pairs within the range (${how}).`);
        }
      } else if (v.hr > 0) warn.push('The spatial-dependence rule also needs the area and number of points.');
      if (v.cont > 0 && A) add('Complexity of terrain', A / (v.cont * 1000), v.wmld > 0 ? v.wmld / 2 : null, A / (2 * v.cont * 1000), 'Coarsest ≤ area ÷ total contour length; recommended = area ÷ (2 × total contour length), half the average contour spacing; finest ≥ narrowest width ÷ 2.');
      if (!rows.length) return U.empty('Enter at least one aspect: a map scale, a positioning error, or the area and number of points. The Example button fills in values from Hengl\'s worked examples.');
      const cs = rows.map(r => r.coarse).filter(x => x > 0), fs = rows.map(r => r.fine).filter(x => x > 0), rs = rows.map(r => r.rec).filter(x => x > 0);
      const coarse = cs.length ? Math.min(...cs) : null, fine = fs.length ? Math.max(...fs) : null;
      let rec = rs.length ? rs.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor((rs.length - 1) / 2)] : null;
      const conflict = fine != null && coarse != null && fine > coarse;
      if (rec != null && !conflict) { if (coarse != null) rec = Math.min(rec, coarse); if (fine != null) rec = Math.max(rec, fine); }
      const inside = NICE.filter(x => x >= (fine ?? 0) * 0.999 && x <= (coarse ?? Infinity) * 1.001);
      const pick = x => (inside.length && !conflict ? inside : NICE).reduce((b, n) => Math.abs(Math.log(n / x)) < Math.abs(Math.log(b / x)) ? n : b);
      const f = x => x == null ? '–' : (x < 10 ? HM.fmt(x, 1) : HM.fmt(x, 0)) + ' m';
      let h = U.big('Recommended resolution', rec != null ? `${pick(rec)} m` : '–', `${rec != null ? f(rec) + ' before rounding to a common grid size. ' : ''}Legible range: ${f(fine)} (finest) to ${f(coarse)} (coarsest).`);
      if (conflict) h += U.note(`<b>The rules conflict:</b> the finest legible resolution (${f(fine)}) is coarser than the coarsest legible one (${f(coarse)}). The datasets don't support each other: for example, positional error or sample spacing too coarse for the map scale or object size you want. Look at which rows set the two limits.`, 'bad');
      h += `<table class="tt"><thead><tr><th>Aspect</th><th class="r">Coarsest ≤</th><th class="r">Finest ≥</th><th class="r">Recommended</th></tr></thead><tbody>` + rows.map(r => `<tr><td>${r.rule}</td><td class="r"${r.coarse === coarse ? ' style="font-weight:700"' : ''}>${f(r.coarse)}</td><td class="r"${r.fine === fine ? ' style="font-weight:700"' : ''}>${f(r.fine)}</td><td class="r">${f(r.rec)}</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody></table>';
      h += U.note('The overall coarsest is the strictest (smallest) coarsest value and the overall finest is the largest finest value (both in bold). The recommendation is the median of the recommended values, kept inside that range, then rounded to the nearest common grid size within it.');
      warn.forEach(w => { h += U.note(w); });
      return { html: h, work: rows.map(r => `<b>${r.rule}.</b> ${r.why}`).concat(['Equations from Table 1 of Hengl, T. (2006). Finding the right pixel size. Computers & Geosciences 32, 1283–1298.']) };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**Reference**

Hengl, T. (2006). Finding the right pixel size. *Computers & Geosciences* 32, 1283–1298. [doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2005.11.008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2005.11.008)
:::

::: {#back-transform .ck-sec}

## Back-transformation

A mean calculated on log values, then exponentiated, is the **median** (geometric mean), not the mean. For skewed soil properties the difference is often 10–30%. Enter what the paper gives on the log scale.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="bt"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  HM.tool({
    id: 'bt', step: 'Log-scale results', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { base: 'ln', c: 0, mu: 0.4, sd: 0.65, rep: 1.49 },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'base', l: 'Logarithm', t: 'seg', d: 'ln', opts: [['ln', 'Natural (ln)'], ['log10', 'Base 10']] },
      { k: 'mu', l: 'Mean of the log values', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'sd', l: 'SD of the log values', t: 'num', w: 3, h: 'For a kriged estimate, use the square root of the kriging variance.' },
      { k: 'c', l: 'Constant added before logging, if log(x + c)', t: 'num', d: 0, w: 3 },
      { k: 'rep', l: 'Value reported in original units (optional)', t: 'num', w: 3 }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      if (v.mu == null || !(v.sd >= 0)) return U.empty('Enter the mean and SD of the log values.');
      const est = (base, mu, sd) => { const k = base === 'ln' ? 1 : Math.LN10; return { med: Math.exp(k * mu) - (v.c || 0), mean: Math.exp(k * mu + (k * sd) ** 2 / 2) - (v.c || 0), lo: Math.exp(k * (mu - 1.96 * sd)) - (v.c || 0), hi: Math.exp(k * (mu + 1.96 * sd)) - (v.c || 0) }; };
      const e = est(v.base, v.mu, v.sd), d = Math.abs(e.mean) < 10 ? 3 : 2;
      let h = U.kv([['Median (geometric mean)', HM.fmt(e.med, d)], ['Mean (arithmetic, lognormal)', HM.fmt(e.mean, d)], ['Mean ÷ median', HM.fmt(e.mean / e.med, 3)], ['Range holding 95% of values', `${HM.fmt(e.lo, d)} – ${HM.fmt(e.hi, d)}`]]);
      if (v.rep > 0) {
        const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) / Math.abs(b) < 0.03;
        if (near(v.rep, e.med)) h = U.note(`<b>The reported ${v.rep} is the median, not the mean.</b> The arithmetic mean is about ${HM.fmt(e.mean, d)}, ${HM.fmt((e.mean / e.med - 1) * 100, 0)}% higher. That matters for totals, stocks and loads, which add up means.`, 'bad') + h;
        else if (near(v.rep, e.mean)) h = U.note(`<b>The reported ${v.rep} is the bias-corrected mean.</b> Correctly back-transformed.`, 'good') + h;
        else {
          const alt = est(v.base === 'ln' ? 'log10' : 'ln', v.mu, v.sd);
          if (near(v.rep, alt.med) || near(v.rep, alt.mean)) h = U.note(`<b>The reported ${v.rep} matches ${v.base === 'ln' ? 'base-10' : 'natural'} logs</b> (${near(v.rep, alt.med) ? 'median' : 'mean'}), not ${v.base === 'ln' ? 'natural' : 'base-10'} logs. Check which logarithm was used.`, 'bad') + h;
          else h = U.note(`The reported ${v.rep} matches neither the median (${HM.fmt(e.med, d)}) nor the mean (${HM.fmt(e.mean, d)}). Check the logarithm base, any constant added before logging, and whether the SD is of the logs or of the original values.`) + h;
        }
      }
      const k = v.base === 'ln' ? 'e' : '10', kk = v.base === 'ln' ? '' : ' × ln 10';
      return { html: h, work: [`Median = ${k}^μ${v.c ? ' − c' : ''} = ${HM.fmt(e.med, d + 1)}`, `Mean = ${k}^(μ + σ²${kk ? '·ln10' : ''}/2)${v.c ? ' − c' : ''} = ${HM.fmt(e.mean, d + 1)}${v.base === 'log10' ? ' (σ is converted to natural-log units first: σ × ln 10)' : ''}`, 'This assumes the log values are roughly normal. For lognormal kriging, the variogram tool applies the full correction, including the Lagrange term.'] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**References**

Aitchison, J., Brown, J.A.C. (1957). *The Lognormal Distribution*. Cambridge University Press.

Journel, A.G. (1980). The lognormal approach to predicting local distributions of selective mining unit grades. *Mathematical Geology* 12, 285–303. [doi:10.1007/BF01029417](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01029417)

Webster, R., Oliver, M.A. (2007). *Geostatistics for Environmental Scientists*, 2nd ed. Wiley.
:::

:::

::: {#stock-arithmetic .ck-sec}

## Carbon stock arithmetic

Rebuild a reported stock from its inputs. If it doesn't match, the check tries the common slips (% vs g/kg, stones ignored or on the wrong basis, organic matter instead of carbon, kg/m² vs Mg/ha) and tells you which one reproduces the reported number.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="sa"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const RHO_G = 2.65; // particle density of coarse fragments, g/cm³
  function stock(p) { // returns Mg C/ha
    const C = p.cunit === 'pct' ? p.c * 10 : p.cunit === 'mgkg' ? p.c / 1000 : p.c;           // g/kg
    const bd = p.bdunit === 'kgm3' ? p.bd / 1000 : p.bd;                                         // g/cm³
    const dep = p.dunit === 'm' ? p.dep * 100 : p.dunit === 'mm' ? p.dep / 10 : p.dep;           // cm
    const cf = (p.cf || 0) / 100;
    let mfe; // g of fine earth per cm³ of whole soil
    if (p.bdbasis === 'whole') mfe = p.cfbasis === 'mass' ? bd * (1 - cf) : bd - cf * RHO_G;
    else { const cfv = p.cfbasis === 'vol' ? cf : (cf / RHO_G) / (cf / RHO_G + (1 - cf) / bd); mfe = bd * (1 - cfv); }
    return { s: C * mfe * dep * 0.1, C, bd, dep, mfe };
  }
  HM.tool({
    id: 'sa', step: 'Inputs as reported', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { c: 1.8, cunit: 'pct', bd: 1.35, bdunit: 'gcm3', bdbasis: 'fine', dep: 30, dunit: 'cm', cf: 15, cfbasis: 'vol', rep: 72.9, repunit: 'mgha' },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'c', l: 'Organic carbon', t: 'num', w: 3 }, { k: 'cunit', l: 'Units', t: 'select', d: 'pct', w: 3, opts: [['pct', '%'], ['gkg', 'g/kg (= mg/g)'], ['mgkg', 'mg/kg']] },
      { k: 'bd', l: 'Bulk density', t: 'num', w: 3 }, { k: 'bdunit', l: 'Units', t: 'select', d: 'gcm3', w: 3, opts: [['gcm3', 'g/cm³ (= Mg/m³)'], ['kgm3', 'kg/m³']] },
      { k: 'bdbasis', l: 'Bulk density is of', t: 'select', d: 'fine', opts: [['fine', 'Fine earth only (stones removed, volume corrected)'], ['whole', 'Whole soil, stones included']] },
      { k: 'dep', l: 'Layer thickness', t: 'num', w: 3 }, { k: 'dunit', l: 'Units', t: 'select', d: 'cm', w: 3, opts: [['cm', 'cm'], ['m', 'm'], ['mm', 'mm']] },
      { k: 'cf', l: 'Coarse fragments (stones, gravel)', t: 'num', d: 0, w: 3, h: '% of the soil.' }, { k: 'cfbasis', l: 'Fragments measured by', t: 'select', d: 'vol', w: 3, opts: [['vol', 'Volume'], ['mass', 'Mass']] },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Reported stock (optional)' },
      { k: 'rep', l: 'Stock', t: 'num', w: 3 }, { k: 'repunit', l: 'Units', t: 'select', d: 'mgha', w: 3, opts: [['mgha', 'Mg C/ha (= t C/ha)'], ['kgm2', 'kg C/m²']] }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      if (!(v.c > 0) || !(v.bd > 0) || !(v.dep > 0) || !(v.cf >= 0 && v.cf < 100)) return U.empty('Enter carbon, bulk density, thickness and coarse fragments.');
      const r = stock(v);
      let h = U.big('Recalculated stock', `${HM.fmt(r.s, 2)} Mg C/ha`, `= ${HM.fmt(r.s / 10, 3)} kg C/m²`);
      const work = [`Carbon = ${HM.fmt(r.C, 3)} g/kg; bulk density = ${HM.fmt(r.bd, 3)} g/cm³; thickness = ${HM.fmt(r.dep, 2)} cm`,
        `Fine earth per volume of soil = ${HM.fmt(r.mfe, 3)} g/cm³ (${v.bdbasis === 'whole' ? 'whole-soil bulk density' : 'fine-earth bulk density'}, fragments by ${v.cfbasis === 'vol' ? 'volume' : 'mass'}${v.cfbasis !== (v.bdbasis === 'whole' ? 'mass' : 'vol') ? `, converted using a stone density of ${RHO_G} g/cm³` : ''})`,
        `Stock = C (g/kg) × fine earth (g/cm³) × thickness (cm) × 0.1 = ${HM.fmt(r.s, 2)} Mg C/ha`];
      if (v.rep > 0) {
        const rep = v.repunit === 'kgm2' ? v.rep * 10 : v.rep, near = x => Math.abs(x - rep) / rep < 0.03;
        if (near(r.s)) h += U.note(`<b>Matches.</b> The reported stock (${HM.fmt(rep, 2)} Mg C/ha) follows from the inputs.`, 'good');
        else {
          const tries = [
            ['% read as g/kg (carbon 10× too low)', { ...v, cunit: v.cunit === 'pct' ? 'gkg' : 'pct' }],
            ['Stones ignored', { ...v, cf: 0 }],
            ['Stone fraction on the wrong basis (volume vs. mass)', { ...v, cfbasis: v.cfbasis === 'vol' ? 'mass' : 'vol' }],
            ['Bulk density on the wrong basis (fine earth vs. whole soil)', { ...v, bdbasis: v.bdbasis === 'fine' ? 'whole' : 'fine' }],
            ['Stones subtracted twice (fine-earth bulk density and a volume correction)', null],
            ['Organic matter used instead of carbon (× 1.724)', { ...v, c: v.c * 1.724 }],
            ['Thickness in mm read as cm, or cm as mm', { ...v, dunit: v.dunit === 'cm' ? 'mm' : 'cm' }]
          ];
          const hits = [];
          tries.forEach(([name, p]) => {
            let val;
            if (p) val = stock(p).s; else val = r.s * (1 - (v.cf || 0) / 100);
            if (isFinite(val) && near(val)) hits.push(`${name}: gives ${HM.fmt(val, 2)}`);
          });
          if (Math.abs(r.s / 10 - rep) / rep < 0.03) hits.push(`The stock is in kg C/m² but labelled Mg C/ha (10× too low)`);
          if (Math.abs(r.s * 10 - rep) / rep < 0.03) hits.push(`The stock is 10× too high: kg C/m² and Mg C/ha mixed up`);
          h += hits.length ? U.note(`<b>Doesn't match (${HM.fmt((rep / r.s - 1) * 100, 0)}% off).</b> This slip reproduces the reported value:<br>• ${hits.join('<br>• ')}`, 'bad')
            : U.note(`<b>Doesn't match (${HM.fmt((rep / r.s - 1) * 100, 0)}% off),</b> and none of the common slips explains it. Check whether the stock is for a different depth, an equivalent soil mass basis, or a sum of several layers.`);
        }
      }
      return { html: h, work };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**References**

Poeplau, C., Vos, C., Don, A. (2017). Soil organic carbon stocks are systematically overestimated by misuse of the parameters bulk density and rock fragment content. *SOIL* 3, 61–66. [doi:10.5194/soil-3-61-2017](https://doi.org/10.5194/soil-3-61-2017)

Pribyl, D.W. (2010). A critical review of the conventional SOC to SOM conversion factor. *Geoderma* 156, 75–83. [doi:10.1016/j.geoderma.2010.02.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2010.02.003)
:::

:::

::: {#area-estimation .ck-sec}

## Area from a confusion matrix

Counting pixels in a map gives biased class areas, because every map has errors. With a stratified accuracy sample, the confusion matrix gives unbiased areas with confidence intervals (Olofsson et al. 2014). Rows are **map** classes, columns are **reference** classes, and the last column is each map class's mapped area.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="oa"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const EX = `class,Deforestation,Gain,Stable forest,Stable non-forest,area
Deforestation,66,0,5,4,200000
Gain,0,55,8,12,150000
Stable forest,1,0,153,11,3200000
Stable non-forest,2,1,9,313,6450000`;
  HM.tool({
    id: 'oa', step: 'Sample counts and mapped areas', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { m: EX, unit: 'px', px: 30 },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'm', l: 'Confusion matrix (comma, semicolon or tab separated)', t: 'textarea', rows: 7, ph: 'class,A,B,C,area\nA,..' },
      { k: 'unit', l: 'Mapped area is in', t: 'select', d: 'ha', w: 3, opts: [['ha', 'hectares'], ['km2', 'km²'], ['px', 'pixels']] },
      { k: 'px', l: 'Pixel size (m)', t: 'num', d: 30, w: 3, show: v => v.unit === 'px' }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const lines = String(v.m || '').trim().split(/\r?\n/).filter(l => l.trim());
      if (lines.length < 3) return U.empty('Paste a matrix with a header row, at least two classes and a final area column. The Example button shows the layout.');
      const sp = l => l.split(/[,;\t]/).map(x => x.trim());
      const head = sp(lines[0]), cls = head.slice(1, -1), k = cls.length;
      const rows = lines.slice(1).map(sp);
      if (rows.length !== k || rows.some(r => r.length !== k + 2)) return U.empty(`Expected ${k} rows of ${k} counts plus an area, matching the ${k} classes in the header.`);
      const n = rows.map(r => r.slice(1, k + 1).map(Number)), A = rows.map(r => Number(r[k + 1]));
      if (n.some(r => r.some(x => !(x >= 0))) || A.some(x => !(x > 0))) return U.empty('Counts must be zero or more and areas above zero.');
      const toHa = v.unit === 'ha' ? 1 : v.unit === 'km2' ? 100 : (v.px * v.px) / 10000;
      const Atot = A.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), W = A.map(a => a / Atot), ni = n.map(r => r.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0));
      if (ni.some(x => x < 2)) return U.empty('Every map class needs at least two sample points.');
      const p = n.map((r, i) => r.map(x => W[i] * x / ni[i]));
      const pj = cls.map((_, j) => p.reduce((s, r) => s + r[j], 0));
      const se = cls.map((_, j) => Math.sqrt(n.reduce((s, r, i) => s + W[i] ** 2 * (r[j] / ni[i]) * (1 - r[j] / ni[i]) / (ni[i] - 1), 0)));
      const Ui = cls.map((_, i) => n[i][i] / ni[i]), seU = Ui.map((u, i) => Math.sqrt(u * (1 - u) / (ni[i] - 1)));
      const OA = pj.reduce((s, _, j) => s + p[j][j], 0), seOA = Math.sqrt(Ui.reduce((s, u, i) => s + W[i] ** 2 * u * (1 - u) / (ni[i] - 1), 0));
      const Nhat = cls.map((_, j) => A.reduce((s, a, i) => s + a * n[i][j] / ni[i], 0));
      const Pj = cls.map((_, j) => p[j][j] / pj[j]);
      const seP = cls.map((_, j) => {
        const term1 = A[j] ** 2 * (1 - Pj[j]) ** 2 * Ui[j] * (1 - Ui[j]) / (ni[j] - 1);
        const term2 = Pj[j] ** 2 * A.reduce((s, a, i) => i === j ? s : s + a ** 2 * (n[i][j] / ni[i]) * (1 - n[i][j] / ni[i]) / (ni[i] - 1), 0);
        return Math.sqrt((term1 + term2)) / Nhat[j];
      });
      const fa = x => HM.fmt(x * toHa, 0);
      let h = `<table class="tt"><thead><tr><th>Class</th><th class="r">Mapped (ha)</th><th class="r">Estimated (ha)</th><th class="r">User's</th><th class="r">Producer's</th></tr></thead><tbody>` +
        cls.map((c, j) => { const est = pj[j] * Atot, ci = 1.96 * se[j] * Atot, diff = (A[j] - est) / est * 100;
          return `<tr><td>${HM.esc(c)}${Math.abs(diff) > 10 ? `<br><span class="tag ${Math.abs(diff) > 25 ? 'bad' : 'warn'}">map ${diff > 0 ? 'over' : 'under'} by ${HM.fmt(Math.abs(diff), 0)}%</span>` : ''}</td><td class="r">${fa(A[j])}</td><td class="r">${fa(est)}<br><span style="color:var(--ink-3)">± ${fa(ci)}</span></td><td class="r">${HM.fmt(Ui[j] * 100, 0)}% ± ${HM.fmt(1.96 * seU[j] * 100, 0)}</td><td class="r">${HM.fmt(Pj[j] * 100, 0)}% ± ${HM.fmt(1.96 * seP[j] * 100, 0)}</td></tr>`; }).join('') + '</tbody></table>';
      h += U.kv([['Overall accuracy', `${HM.fmt(OA * 100, 1)}% ± ${HM.fmt(1.96 * seOA * 100, 1)}`], ['Total area', `${fa(Atot)} ha`]]);
      h += U.note('± values are 95% confidence intervals. Estimated areas correct the pixel count for the errors in the map; report these, not mapped areas, along with their intervals. The method assumes the sample was stratified by map class (or random).');
      return { html: h, work: [`Weights W = mapped area of each map class ÷ total`, `Estimated proportion p(i,j) = W(i) × n(i,j) ÷ n(i·); class area = total area × Σᵢ p(i,j)`, `Standard error of each area proportion = √Σᵢ W(i)² × (n(i,j)/n(i·)) × (1 − n(i,j)/n(i·)) ÷ (n(i·) − 1)`, 'Accuracy standard errors follow Olofsson et al. (2014), Remote Sensing of Environment 148, 42–57.'] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**Reference**

Olofsson, P., Foody, G.M., Herold, M., Stehman, S.V., Woodcock, C.E., Wulder, M.A. (2014). Good practices for estimating area and assessing accuracy of land change. *Remote Sensing of Environment* 148, 42–57. [doi:10.1016/j.rse.2014.02.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2014.02.015)
:::

:::

::: {#effective-sample-size .ck-sec}

## Effective sample size

Samples close together carry overlapping information. For estimating an average, a cluster of ten nearby samples can be worth little more than one. This uses the variogram to work out how many independent samples your layout is really worth.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="es"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const F = { sph: (h, r) => h >= r ? 1 : 1.5 * h / r - 0.5 * (h / r) ** 3, exp: (h, r) => 1 - Math.exp(-3 * h / r), gau: (h, r) => 1 - Math.exp(-3 * (h / r) ** 2) };
  let ex = 'x,y'; const s = [[100, 100], [600, 150], [350, 500], [800, 700], [150, 850]];
  let seed = 7; const rnd = () => (seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
  s.forEach(c => { for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) ex += `\n${Math.round(c[0] + (rnd() - 0.5) * 40)},${Math.round(c[1] + (rnd() - 0.5) * 40)}`; });
  HM.tool({
    id: 'es', step: 'Sample locations and variogram', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { xy: ex, model: 'sph', nug: 20, r: 200 },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'xy', l: 'Coordinates, one sample per line: x, y (metres)', t: 'textarea', rows: 6, ph: 'x,y\n120,340\n135,352' },
      { k: 'model', l: 'Variogram model', t: 'select', d: 'sph', w: 2, opts: [['sph', 'Spherical'], ['exp', 'Exponential'], ['gau', 'Gaussian']] },
      { k: 'nug', l: 'Nugget (% of sill)', t: 'num', d: 20, w: 2 },
      { k: 'r', l: 'Range, practical (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const pts = String(v.xy || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.split(/[,;\t\s]+/).map(Number)).filter(q => q.length >= 2 && isFinite(q[0]) && isFinite(q[1]));
      if (pts.length < 3 || !(v.r > 0) || !(v.nug >= 0 && v.nug <= 100)) return U.empty('Enter at least three coordinate pairs, the nugget and the range.');
      const n = pts.length, c1 = 1 - v.nug / 100, f = F[v.model];
      const rho = (a, b) => { const d = Math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1]); return d === 0 ? (a === b ? 1 : c1) : c1 * (1 - f(d, v.r)); };
      const sumRho = P => { let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < P.length; i++) for (let j = 0; j < P.length; j++) s += i === j ? 1 : rho(P[i], P[j]); return s; };
      const S = sumRho(pts), neff = n * n / S;
      const xs = pts.map(q => q[0]), ys = pts.map(q => q[1]), w = Math.max(...xs) - Math.min(...xs), hgt = Math.max(...ys) - Math.min(...ys);
      const kx = Math.max(1, Math.round(Math.sqrt(n * (w || 1) / (hgt || 1)))), ky = Math.max(1, Math.round(n / kx)), grid = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < kx; i++) for (let j = 0; j < ky; j++) grid.push([Math.min(...xs) + (i + 0.5) * (w || 1) / kx, Math.min(...ys) + (j + 0.5) * (hgt || 1) / ky]);
      const ng = grid.length, neffG = ng * ng / sumRho(grid);
      let h = U.big('Effective sample size', HM.fmt(neff, 1), `out of ${n} samples: each is worth about ${HM.fmt(neff / n, 2)} of an independent sample.`);
      h += U.kv([['Same number spread on a grid over the same area', `${HM.fmt(neffG * n / ng, 1)} effective`], ['Standard error of the mean, vs. assuming independence', `${HM.fmt(Math.sqrt(n / neff), 2)}× larger`]]);
      if (neff / n < 0.5) h += U.note(`Clustering costs a lot here. Confidence intervals that treat the ${n} samples as independent are about ${HM.fmt(Math.sqrt(n / neff), 1)}× too narrow, and tests will find "significant" differences too easily.`, 'bad');
      return { html: h, work: [`Correlation between two samples = (1 − nugget share) × (1 − variogram shape at their distance); 1 for a sample with itself`, `Effective n = n² ÷ ΣΣ correlation = ${n}² ÷ ${HM.fmt(S, 1)} = ${HM.fmt(neff, 2)}`, 'This is for estimating a mean by simple averaging; kriging weights would recover a little more information.'] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**References**

Cressie, N.A.C. (1993). *Statistics for Spatial Data*, revised ed. Wiley. Section 1.3.

Webster, R., Oliver, M.A. (2007). *Geostatistics for Environmental Scientists*, 2nd ed. Wiley.
:::

:::

::: {#spatial-cv .ck-sec}

## Spatial cross-validation and leakage

Random cross-validation on spatial data usually tests points close to the training data, so it reports accuracy the map won't achieve between samples. Tick anything that applies to the study you're checking.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="cv"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const ITEMS = [
    ['rand', 'Random k-fold or leave-one-out cross-validation on clustered or densely sampled points', 'Test points sit next to training points. Use spatial block CV, buffered leave-one-out, or NNDM (Milà et al. 2022) so test distances match prediction distances.'],
    ['prof', 'Horizons or depths from the same profile are split between training and test folds', 'Layers of one profile are strongly related. Keep whole profiles (or sites) in the same fold.'],
    ['rep', 'Repeat measurements of the same sites (different years or replicates) are split across folds', 'The model is tested on sites it has already seen. Group folds by site.'],
    ['pre', 'Feature selection, scaling, outlier removal or covariate tuning was done on the full dataset before splitting', 'Information from the test data leaks into the model. Do every data-driven step inside each training fold.'],
    ['tune', 'Hyperparameters were tuned on the same folds used to report accuracy', 'The reported accuracy is optimistic. Use nested CV or a separate test set.'],
    ['target', 'A covariate was derived from the target or from the same samples (for example an existing map made with these points)', 'The model can recover the answer from the covariate. Remove it, or show it was independent.'],
    ['scope', 'Validation data come from the same area or campaign, but the map is claimed for a wider area or another time', 'Accuracy doesn\'t transfer automatically. Validate in the target area, or limit the claim (area of applicability, Meyer & Pebesma 2021).'],
    ['dup', 'Duplicate or near-duplicate coordinates exist across folds', 'Identical locations in training and test inflate accuracy. Merge or group them.'],
    ['fit', 'Accuracy is reported on calibration data ("fitted vs. observed")', 'That is goodness of fit, not prediction accuracy. Ask for independent or cross-validated results.']
  ];
  HM.tool({
    id: 'cv', step: 'What applies to your study', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { rand: true, pre: true, dcv: 40, dpred: 380, r: 250 },
    inputs: ITEMS.map(([k, l]) => ({ k, l, t: 'check', d: false })).concat([
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Distances (optional)', h: 'If you know them: the typical distance from each test point to its nearest training point in the cross-validation, and from map pixels to their nearest sample.' },
      { k: 'dcv', l: 'Test → nearest training (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'dpred', l: 'Map pixel → nearest sample (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'r', l: 'Variogram range (m)', t: 'num', w: 2 }
    ]),
    compute(v, U) {
      const hit = ITEMS.filter(([k]) => v[k]);
      let distNote = '';
      if (v.dcv > 0 && v.dpred > 0) {
        const ratio = v.dpred / v.dcv;
        if (v.r > 0 && v.dcv < v.r && v.dpred > v.r) distNote = U.note(`<b>Cross-validation tests inside the range; the map predicts beyond it.</b> Test points are about ${HM.fmt(v.dcv, 0)} m from training data, within the ${HM.fmt(v.r, 0)} m range where neighbours help, but map pixels are typically ${HM.fmt(v.dpred, 0)} m away, beyond it. The reported accuracy won't hold across most of the map.`, 'bad');
        else if (ratio > 2) distNote = U.note(`<b>Test points are ${HM.fmt(ratio, 1)}× closer to training data than map pixels are to samples.</b> The cross-validation is likely optimistic.`, 'bad');
        else distNote = U.note('Test distances are similar to prediction distances: the validation reflects how the map is used.', 'good');
      }
      const level = hit.length === 0 && !distNote.includes('bad') ? ['good', 'No warning signs ticked'] : hit.length <= 1 ? ['warn', 'Some risk of optimistic accuracy'] : ['bad', 'High risk of optimistic accuracy'];
      return `<p><span class="tag ${level[0]}">${level[1]}</span></p>` + distNote + (hit.length ? `<h3>Questions reviewers might ask</h3><ul class="plain">${hit.map(([, l, fix]) => `<li><b>${l}.</b> ${fix}</li>`).join('')}</ul>` : '');
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**References**

Roberts, D.R. et al. (2017). Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. *Ecography* 40, 913–929. [doi:10.1111/ecog.02881](https://doi.org/10.1111/ecog.02881)

Meyer, H., Pebesma, E. (2021). Predicting into unknown space? Estimating the area of applicability of spatial prediction models. *Methods in Ecology and Evolution* 12, 1620–1633. [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13650](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13650)

Milà, C., Mateu, J., Pebesma, E., Meyer, H. (2022). Nearest neighbour distance matching leave-one-out cross-validation for map validation. *Methods in Ecology and Evolution* 13, 1304–1316. [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13851](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13851)
:::

:::

::: {#independence .ck-sec}

## Independence and study design <span class="ck-beta">BETA</span>

Independence is a property of the study design and the question being asked, not a box that a single diagnostic can certify. Use this guided check to identify common sources of dependence and mismatches between the sampling unit, statistical analysis, and validation design. It flags issues to investigate; it does not automatically invalidate a study. If you know how many observations and groups there are, it also shows how much the grouping shrinks the effective sample size.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="indep"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const structureOptions = [
    ['none', 'No obvious grouping or repeated observations'],
    ['group', 'Observations grouped within sites, plots, subjects, catchments, batches, etc.'],
    ['repeat', 'Repeated measurements of the same units (time, depth, treatment, or replicate)'],
    ['space', 'Spatially located observations with possible spatial dependence'],
    ['time', 'Ordered time series or observations close together in time'],
    ['multi', 'More than one structure (e.g. repeated measurements within spatial sites)']
  ];
  const goalOptions = [
    ['describe', 'Describe or compare the sampled units'],
    ['population', 'Infer a population mean, difference, or relationship'],
    ['predict', 'Predict new observations in the same sampled setting'],
    ['newgroup', 'Predict for new sites, subjects, regions, or groups'],
    ['future', 'Predict future observations']
  ];
  const splitOptions = [
    ['na', 'Not a predictive modelling study / not applicable'],
    ['random', 'Random train/test split or random cross-validation'],
    ['group', 'Groups or sites kept wholly in one fold'],
    ['space', 'Spatial blocks, spatial buffers, or distance-matched validation'],
    ['time', 'Forward-chaining or time-ordered validation'],
    ['external', 'Independent external dataset or campaign']
  ];
  HM.tool({
    id: 'indep', step: 'Study structure and intended inference', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { structure: 'multi', unit: 'profile', goal: 'newgroup', split: 'random', groups: true, pseudorep: true, overlap: true, leakage: false, balanced: false, nobs: 240, ngrp: 30, icc: 0.4 },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'structure', l: 'What structure is present in the observations?', t: 'select', d: 'none', opts: structureOptions },
      { k: 'unit', l: 'What is the independent sampling or experimental unit?', t: 'select', d: 'sample', opts: [['sample', 'Each individual observation'], ['plot', 'Plot, site, subject, or other group'], ['profile', 'Profile, core, or sampling location'], ['cluster', 'Catchment, region, school, clinic, or higher-level cluster'], ['timeunit', 'Time point or time block'], ['unclear', 'Not stated or unclear']] },
      { k: 'goal', l: 'What is the main inferential or prediction goal?', t: 'select', d: 'population', opts: goalOptions },
      { k: 'split', l: 'If predicting, how was validation separated?', t: 'select', d: 'na', opts: splitOptions },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Potential issues reported or visible in the paper' },
      { k: 'groups', l: 'Several observations come from the same group, site, subject, profile, or experimental unit', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'pseudorep', l: 'The analysis appears to count subsamples, repeated measures, pixels, or technical replicates as independent replicates', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'overlap', l: 'Nearby locations, adjacent time points, or related observations may occur in both training and test data', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'leakage', l: 'Preprocessing, feature selection, tuning, or covariate construction may have used information from the held-out data', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'balanced', l: 'The paper reports a design-aware method (e.g. mixed model, cluster-robust SE, block design, or grouped validation)', t: 'check', d: false },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Numbers, if known (optional): how much the grouping costs' },
      { k: 'nobs', l: 'Observations analysed', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'ngrp', l: 'Independent groups (sites, profiles, subjects…)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'icc', l: 'Intraclass correlation (ICC, 0–1), if reported', t: 'num', w: 2 }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const findings = [];
      const add = (level, title, detail) => findings.push({level, title, detail});
      // design effect (Kish 1965): DEFF = 1 + (m - 1) * ICC, m = mean group size
      const given = x => x !== '' && x !== null && x !== undefined && isFinite(Number(x));
      const nn = Number(v.nobs), kk = Number(v.ngrp), icc = Number(v.icc);
      let numHtml = '', numWork = [];
      if (given(v.nobs) && given(v.ngrp) && nn > 0 && kk > 0 && kk <= nn) {
        const m = nn / kk;
        const neffOf = r => nn / (1 + (m - 1) * r);
        if (given(v.icc) && icc >= 0 && icc <= 1) {
          const deff = 1 + (m - 1) * icc, neff = nn / deff;
          numHtml = U.big('Effective sample size', HM.fmt(neff, 1), `out of ${nn} observations in ${kk} groups (about ${HM.fmt(m, 1)} per group), with ICC ${HM.fmt(icc, 2)}.`)
            + U.kv([['Design effect', HM.fmt(deff, 2)], ['Standard errors that ignore the grouping are too small by', `${HM.fmt(Math.sqrt(deff), 2)}×`], ['Effective n lies between', `${kk} (groups) and ${nn} (observations)`]]);
          if (neff < nn / 2) add('high', 'Grouping removes most of the apparent replication', `With this ICC the ${nn} observations carry about as much information as ${HM.fmt(neff, 0)} independent ones. Tests and intervals that use n = ${nn} will look far more certain than the data support.`);
          numWork = [`Mean group size m = ${nn} ÷ ${kk} = ${HM.fmt(m, 2)}`, `Design effect = 1 + (m − 1) × ICC = 1 + ${HM.fmt(m - 1, 2)} × ${HM.fmt(icc, 2)} = ${HM.fmt(deff, 3)}`, `Effective n = ${nn} ÷ ${HM.fmt(deff, 3)} = ${HM.fmt(neff, 1)}`];
        } else {
          const rows = [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8].map(r => [`ICC ${r}`, `${HM.fmt(neffOf(r), 1)} effective (standard errors ${HM.fmt(Math.sqrt(1 + (m - 1) * r), 2)}× too small)`]);
          numHtml = '<h3>Effective sample size for a range of ICC values</h3>' + U.kv(rows)
            + `<p>Effective n lies between ${kk} (the number of groups) and ${nn} (the number of observations). Soil properties measured repeatedly within a profile or site often have ICCs well above 0.3.</p>`;
          numWork = [`Mean group size m = ${nn} ÷ ${kk} = ${HM.fmt(m, 2)}; design effect = 1 + (m − 1) × ICC for each ICC shown`];
        }
        numWork.push('This is the Kish design effect for estimating a mean with groups of similar size. For a regression slope it also depends on how strongly the predictor itself clusters (Moulton 1990); unequal group sizes raise it further.');
        if (v.unit === 'sample' && kk < nn) add('warn', 'The stated unit may be wrong', `You gave ${kk} groups for ${nn} observations, but chose “each individual observation” as the independent unit. If the observations within a group are related, the group is the independent unit.`);
      } else if (given(v.nobs) || given(v.ngrp)) {
        numHtml = U.note('Enter both the number of observations and the number of groups (groups no more than observations) to see the effective sample size.', 'warn');
      }
      if (v.unit === 'unclear') add('warn', 'Independent unit is unclear', 'The paper should identify the unit independently sampled or assigned to treatment. The number of measurements is not necessarily the number of independent replicates.');
      if (v.groups || ['group','repeat','multi'].includes(v.structure)) {
        if (v.balanced) add('info', 'Grouped or repeated data: check the stated adjustment', 'The paper reports a design-aware method. Confirm that it matches the grouping structure and the estimand; a mixed model or robust standard error does not automatically solve every dependence problem.');
        else add('warn', 'Grouped or repeated observations may be dependent', 'Check whether inference accounts for the group or repeated-measure structure. Possible approaches include group-level summaries, mixed-effects models, GEE, cluster-robust uncertainty, or a design-specific repeated-measures analysis. The appropriate choice depends on the question and design.');
      }
      if (v.pseudorep) add('high', 'Possible pseudoreplication', 'Check whether treatment or sampling was independently replicated at the level claimed. Subsamples and technical replicates can improve measurement precision, but do not create additional independent experimental units.');
      if (['space','multi'].includes(v.structure)) {
        if (v.goal === 'newgroup' && v.split !== 'space' && v.split !== 'external') add('high', 'Validation may not match prediction to new places', 'For a claim about new sites or regions, random folds can place nearby observations in training and test sets. Consider spatial blocking, buffers, distance-matched validation, or an independent target-area dataset.');
        else add('warn', 'Check spatial dependence against the analysis goal', 'Spatial autocorrelation does not by itself make an analysis invalid. Check whether residual dependence affects standard errors or whether validation distances represent the locations where predictions will be used.');
      }
      if (['time','multi'].includes(v.structure)) {
        if (v.goal === 'future' && v.split !== 'time' && v.split !== 'external') add('high', 'Validation may use information from the future', 'For forecasting, random splits can allow future observations to inform predictions of earlier periods. Use time-ordered evaluation, ideally preserving the forecast horizon and any temporal grouping.');
        else add('warn', 'Check temporal dependence and ordering', 'Adjacent time points or repeated measurements may be correlated. Confirm that the uncertainty model accounts for dependence and that any validation preserves the intended time direction.');
      }
      if (v.overlap) add('high', 'Potential train–test dependence', 'Check whether related observations, nearby points, repeated measures, profiles, or duplicate coordinates cross the training/test boundary. Choose grouping or spatial/temporal separation to match the intended deployment setting.');
      if (v.leakage) add('high', 'Potential information leakage', 'All data-driven preprocessing, feature selection, imputation, scaling, and tuning should be fitted using training data only within each resampling split. Target-derived covariates need particular scrutiny.');
      if (v.goal === 'newgroup' && v.split === 'random') add('high', 'Random validation may answer the wrong question', 'Random validation estimates performance for data resembling the sampled dataset, often with represented groups in both sets. It does not establish performance at genuinely new sites, subjects, or regions.');
      if (v.goal === 'future' && v.split === 'random') add('high', 'Random validation is usually unsuitable for forecasting', 'A random split can mix past and future information. Prefer a time-ordered split or rolling-origin evaluation that mimics the actual forecast task.');
      if (v.structure === 'none' && !v.groups && !v.pseudorep && !v.overlap && !v.leakage) add('info', 'No obvious dependence issue selected', 'This is not proof of independence. Confirm that the sampling design, residual structure, and data-processing workflow support the assumption for the specific analysis.');
      if (v.split === 'group' && v.goal === 'newgroup') add('info', 'Grouped validation is aligned in principle', 'Keeping entire groups out of training is generally appropriate when the target is new groups. Check that the groups correspond to the real deployment unit and that enough independent groups are held out.');
      if (v.split === 'space' && ['space','multi'].includes(v.structure)) add('info', 'Spatially separated validation selected', 'Confirm that block size or buffer distance is justified by the spatial structure and matches the distances expected at prediction time. Spatial blocking is not automatically sufficient if blocks are too small or the target region differs.');
      if (v.split === 'time' && ['time','multi'].includes(v.structure)) add('info', 'Time-ordered validation selected', 'Confirm that all preprocessing and tuning occur within each training window and that the evaluation reflects the intended forecast horizon.');
      const rank = {high: 0, warn: 1, info: 2};
      findings.sort((a,b) => rank[a.level] - rank[b.level]);
      const label = findings.some(x => x.level === 'high') ? ['bad','Potential design mismatch or leakage to investigate'] : findings.some(x => x.level === 'warn') ? ['warn','Independence assumptions need a closer look'] : ['good','No major warning selected; verify against the paper'];
      let html = `<p><span class="tag ${label[0]}">${label[1]}</span></p>`;
      html += '<p>This is a guided screening result based on the selections above, not a statistical test of independence.</p>';
      html += numHtml;
      html += findings.map(f => U.note(`<b>${f.title}.</b> ${f.detail}`, f.level === 'high' ? 'bad' : f.level === 'warn' ? 'warn' : 'good')).join('');
      html += '<h3>Questions reviewers might ask</h3><ul class="plain"><li>What is the independently sampled or randomised unit?</li><li>Does the statistical model account for dependence at that unit?</li><li>Does the validation split mimic the population, location, group, or time period to which the conclusions are intended to apply?</li><li>Were all data-dependent modelling decisions confined to the training data?</li></ul>';
      return { html, work: [
        ...numWork,
        'Independence is design- and estimand-specific. A dependence structure may affect standard errors, effective sample size, or predictive validation in different ways; these are related but not interchangeable issues.',
        'The checklist reports potential risks from user-selected study characteristics. It does not estimate correlation, effective sample size, or the magnitude of bias.',
        'For spatial data, select validation separation based on the prediction task and expected distance to training observations. For forecasting, preserve temporal order. For grouped data, keep the relevant independent groups together.',
        'A lack of detected dependence is not evidence that observations are independent. Review the design, residuals, and analysis assumptions.'
      ] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

Meyer, H., Pebesma, E. (2021). Predicting into unknown space? Estimating the area of applicability of spatial prediction models. *Methods in Ecology and Evolution* 12, 1620–1633. [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13650](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13650)

Kish, L. (1965). *Survey Sampling*. Wiley, New York.

Moulton, B.R. (1990). An illustration of a pitfall in estimating the effects of aggregate variables on micro units. *Review of Economics and Statistics* 72, 334–338. [doi:10.2307/2109724](https://doi.org/10.2307/2109724)
