::: {#assumptions-check .ck-sec}

## Statistical assumptions check <span class="ck-beta">BETA</span>

A guided check for matching assumptions to the statistical method. Select the method and the diagnostics you have checked, then use the prompts to identify anything that may need further investigation. If you have the residuals, paste them: the check reports skewness, outliers, unequal spread, curvature and, for ordered data, autocorrelation, with a residual plot. Reviewers might ask similar questions about the evidence reported.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="assump"></div>
<script>
/* Shared statistics helpers for the checks below (normal, t, exact binomial). */
window.CKSTAT = window.CKSTAT || (function () {
  const lgamma = z => {
    const c = [0.99999999999980993, 676.5203681218851, -1259.1392167224028, 771.32342877765313, -176.61502916214059, 12.507343278686905, -0.13857109526572012, 9.9843695780195716e-6, 1.5056327351493116e-7];
    if (z < 0.5) return Math.log(Math.PI / Math.abs(Math.sin(Math.PI * z))) - lgamma(1 - z);
    z -= 1; let x = c[0]; for (let i = 1; i < 9; i++) x += c[i] / (z + i);
    const t = z + 7.5; return 0.5 * Math.log(2 * Math.PI) + (z + 0.5) * Math.log(t) - t + Math.log(x);
  };
  const betacf = (a, b, x) => {
    const FP = 1e-300; let qab = a + b, qap = a + 1, qam = a - 1, c = 1, d = 1 - qab * x / qap;
    if (Math.abs(d) < FP) d = FP; d = 1 / d; let h = d;
    for (let m = 1; m <= 300; m++) {
      const m2 = 2 * m; let aa = m * (b - m) * x / ((qam + m2) * (a + m2));
      d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < FP) d = FP; c = 1 + aa / c; if (Math.abs(c) < FP) c = FP; d = 1 / d; h *= d * c;
      aa = -(a + m) * (qab + m) * x / ((a + m2) * (qap + m2));
      d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < FP) d = FP; c = 1 + aa / c; if (Math.abs(c) < FP) c = FP; d = 1 / d;
      const del = d * c; h *= del; if (Math.abs(del - 1) < 3e-14) break;
    }
    return h;
  };
  const ibeta = (x, a, b) => {
    if (x <= 0) return 0; if (x >= 1) return 1;
    const bt = Math.exp(lgamma(a + b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) + a * Math.log(x) + b * Math.log(1 - x));
    return x < (a + 1) / (a + b + 2) ? bt * betacf(a, b, x) / a : 1 - bt * betacf(b, a, 1 - x) / b;
  };
  const erf = x => { const s = Math.sign(x); x = Math.abs(x); const t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x);
    return s * (1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x)); };
  const normCdf = z => 0.5 * (1 + erf(z / Math.SQRT2));
  const tTwoSided = (t, df) => ibeta(df / (df + t * t), df / 2, 0.5);
  const binomTwoSided = (k, n) => { // exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.5
    if (n === 0) return 1; const lo = Math.min(k, n - k); let s = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= lo; i++) s += Math.exp(lgamma(n + 1) - lgamma(i + 1) - lgamma(n - i + 1) - n * Math.LN2);
    return Math.min(1, 2 * s);
  };
  const ranks = a => { const o = a.map((v, i) => [v, i]).sort((p, q) => p[0] - q[0]), r = new Array(a.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < o.length;) { let j = i; while (j + 1 < o.length && o[j + 1][0] === o[i][0]) j++; for (let k = i; k <= j; k++) r[o[k][1]] = (i + j) / 2 + 1; i = j + 1; } return r; };
  const pearson = (x, y) => { const n = x.length, mx = x.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / n, my = y.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / n;
    let sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { sxy += (x[i] - mx) * (y[i] - my); sxx += (x[i] - mx) ** 2; syy += (y[i] - my) ** 2; }
    return sxx > 0 && syy > 0 ? sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy) : 0; };
  const fmtP = p => p < 0.001 ? 'p < 0.001' : 'p = ' + p.toFixed(3);
  const parseRows = txt => String(txt || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l && !/^[a-z]/i.test(l))
    .map(l => l.split(/[,;\t\s]+/).map(Number)).filter(r => r.length && r.every(isFinite));
  return { lgamma, ibeta, normCdf, tTwoSided, binomTwoSided, ranks, pearson, fmtP, parseRows };
})();

(function () {
  const S = window.CKSTAT;
  const methods = [['linear', 'Linear regression / ANCOVA'], ['anova', 'ANOVA / group comparison'], ['logistic', 'Logistic regression'], ['correlation', 'Pearson correlation'], ['mixed', 'Mixed-effects / repeated measures'], ['nonparam', 'Rank-based / nonparametric method'], ['other', 'Other or unclear']];
  const names = { resid: 'Residual or model diagnostics', vari: 'Variance / dispersion', dist: 'Distributional assumption', infl: 'Influential observations', ind: 'Independence / grouping', form: 'Functional form / link' };
  // example: a regression whose residual spread grows with the fitted value
  let seed = 11; const rnd = () => (seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
  const gauss = () => Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(rnd())) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * rnd());
  let ex = 'fitted,residual'; for (let i = 0; i < 70; i++) { const f = 1 + i * 0.3; ex += `\n${f.toFixed(2)},${(gauss() * 0.15 * f).toFixed(3)}`; }

  HM.tool({
    id: 'assump', step: 'Method, aim and the checks reported', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { method: 'linear', aim: 'inference', resid: true, vari: false, dist: true, infl: false, ind: false, form: true, data: ex, ordered: false },
    inputs: [
      { k: 'method', l: 'Method reported', t: 'select', d: 'linear', opts: methods },
      { k: 'aim', l: 'Primary aim', t: 'select', d: 'inference', opts: [['inference', 'Inference (tests, estimates or confidence intervals)'], ['prediction', 'Prediction'], ['description', 'Description / exploration']] },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Which checks have you carried out or documented?' },
      { k: 'resid', l: 'Residuals or model diagnostics inspected', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'vari', l: 'Variance / dispersion assessed', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'dist', l: 'Relevant distributional assumption assessed', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'infl', l: 'Influential points / outliers assessed where relevant', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'ind', l: 'Independence or grouping structure addressed', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'form', l: 'Functional form / link / linearity assessed where relevant', t: 'check', d: false },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Residuals (optional): paste them for a quick diagnostic' },
      { k: 'data', l: 'One per line: residual, or fitted, residual. A header row is ignored.', t: 'textarea', rows: 6, ph: 'fitted,residual\n12.1,0.84\n13.4,-1.10' },
      { k: 'ordered', l: 'Rows are in time order or along a transect (checks autocorrelation)', t: 'check', d: false }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const m = v.method, aim = v.aim, keys = Object.keys(names);
      const done = keys.filter(k => v[k]), missing = keys.filter(k => !v[k]);
      const relevant = [];
      if (['linear', 'anova', 'mixed'].includes(m)) relevant.push('Check whether the model’s error structure and variance assumptions are appropriate for the design. Normality, where needed for inference, concerns the model errors or residuals—not automatically the raw response.');
      if (m === 'linear') relevant.push('Check linearity / functional form, residual-versus-fitted structure, heteroscedasticity, leverage and influential observations.');
      if (m === 'anova') relevant.push('Check independence at the experimental-unit level and whether variance homogeneity is plausible; the appropriate response to unequal variance depends on the design and method.');
      if (m === 'logistic') relevant.push('Check the binary outcome and link specification, functional form for continuous predictors on the logit scale, separation, influential observations, and overdispersion where relevant. Normal residuals are not a standard logistic-regression requirement.');
      if (m === 'correlation') relevant.push('For Pearson correlation, inspect linearity, influential points, and whether the inference accounts for dependence. Distributional assumptions depend on the inferential procedure; a scatterplot is essential.');
      if (m === 'mixed') relevant.push('Identify the grouping / random-effects structure and check whether it matches the sampling or repeated-measures design. Residual and random-effect diagnostics answer different questions.');
      if (m === 'nonparam') relevant.push('Do not assume “nonparametric” means assumption-free. Check independence, measurement scale, sampling design, and the specific method’s assumptions (for example, shape assumptions for some rank-based comparisons).');
      if (m === 'other') relevant.push('The method is too broad to prescribe a valid assumption set. Identify the exact estimator, test, likelihood or algorithm before deciding which diagnostics are required.');
      if (aim === 'prediction') relevant.push('For prediction, prioritise out-of-sample performance, calibration, distribution shift and leakage. A diagnostic that supports coefficient inference may not establish predictive performance.');
      if (aim === 'description') relevant.push('For descriptive or exploratory work, distinguish assumptions needed for the reported summaries from assumptions needed for formal uncertainty or generalisation.');

      let html = '<p><span class="tag warn">Guided check — not an automated verdict</span></p>';
      html += '<h3>Method-specific prompts</h3><ul>' + relevant.map(x => '<li>' + x + '</li>').join('') + '</ul>';
      html += '<h3>Checks not marked as reported</h3>' + (missing.length ? '<ul>' + missing.map(k => '<li><strong>' + names[k] + ':</strong> confirm whether this is relevant to the chosen method and whether the paper reports adequate evidence. An unchecked item is not proof the authors omitted it.</li>').join('') + '</ul>' : '<p>All checklist items were marked. Verify that the paper reports suitable evidence rather than only stating that checks were performed.</p>');
      html += '<p><strong>Marked as reported:</strong> ' + (done.length ? done.map(k => names[k]).join('; ') : 'none') + '.</p>';
      const work = ['Interpretation depends on the estimator, design, sample size and inferential target. Do not require every diagnostic for every method.'];

      // ---- optional residual diagnostics ----
      const rows = S.parseRows(v.data);
      if (rows.length) {
        const two = rows.every(r => r.length >= 2), fit = two ? rows.map(r => r[0]) : null, e = rows.map(r => two ? r[1] : r[0]);
        const n = e.length;
        if (n < 8) {
          html += U.note('Paste at least 8 residuals for the diagnostic.', 'warn');
        } else {
          const mean = e.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0) / n, sd = Math.sqrt(e.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - mean) ** 2, 0) / (n - 1));
          const m2 = e.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - mean) ** 2, 0) / n, m3 = e.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - mean) ** 3, 0) / n, m4 = e.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - mean) ** 4, 0) / n;
          const g1 = m3 / m2 ** 1.5, g2 = m4 / m2 ** 2 - 3, jb = n / 6 * (g1 * g1 + g2 * g2 / 4), pjb = Math.exp(-jb / 2);
          const z = e.map(x => (x - mean) / sd), out = z.filter(x => Math.abs(x) > 3).length, expOut = 0.0027 * n;
          const kv = [['Residuals', `${n}`], ['Mean (should be near 0)', `${HM.fmt(mean, 3)} (${HM.fmt(sd > 0 ? mean / sd : 0, 2)} SD)`], ['Skewness', HM.fmt(g1, 2)], ['Excess kurtosis', HM.fmt(g2, 2)], ['Jarque–Bera normality test', `${S.fmtP(pjb)}`], ['Beyond ±3 SD', `${out} (about ${HM.fmt(expOut, 1)} expected if normal)`]];
          const flags = [];
          if (Math.abs(g1) > 1 || Math.abs(g2) > 2) flags.push(['warn', `The residuals are ${Math.abs(g1) > 1 ? (g1 > 0 ? 'strongly right-skewed' : 'strongly left-skewed') : 'heavy-tailed'}. For small samples this affects tests and intervals; a transformation, a different error distribution or robust methods may fit better.`]);
          if (pjb < 0.05 && n >= 200) flags.push(['good', `The normality test rejects (${S.fmtP(pjb)}), but with ${n} residuals it detects departures too small to matter. Judge by the skewness, kurtosis and plot instead.`]);
          else if (pjb < 0.05) flags.push(['warn', `The normality test rejects (${S.fmtP(pjb)}). With ${n} residuals this matters for tests and intervals that assume normal errors.`]);
          else if (n < 30) flags.push(['good', `No departure from normality detected, but with only ${n} residuals the test has little power. Look at the plot.`]);
          if (out > Math.max(1, 3 * expOut)) flags.push(['warn', `${out} residuals lie beyond ±3 SD, more than a normal distribution would give. Check them for data errors and their influence on the fit.`]);
          if (fit) {
            const rho = S.pearson(S.ranks(fit), S.ranks(e.map(Math.abs))), zr = rho * Math.sqrt(n - 1), pr = 2 * (1 - S.normCdf(Math.abs(zr)));
            kv.push(['Spread vs fitted value (Spearman ρ of |residual|)', `${HM.fmt(rho, 2)}, ${S.fmtP(pr)}`]);
            if (pr < 0.05 && Math.abs(rho) > 0.2) flags.push(['warn', `The spread of the residuals ${rho > 0 ? 'grows' : 'shrinks'} with the fitted value (ρ = ${HM.fmt(rho, 2)}). Standard errors that assume constant variance will be wrong; consider a transformation, weights or heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors.`]);
            const ord = fit.map((f, i) => [f, e[i]]).sort((p, q) => p[0] - q[0]), k3 = Math.floor(n / 3);
            const thirds = [ord.slice(0, k3), ord.slice(k3, n - k3), ord.slice(n - k3)].map(g => g.reduce((s, p) => s + p[1], 0) / g.length);
            kv.push(['Mean residual: low / middle / high fitted thirds', thirds.map(t => HM.fmt(t, 2)).join(' / ')]);
            if (thirds.some(t => Math.abs(t) > 0.5 * sd)) flags.push(['warn', 'The mean residual differs between the low, middle and high fitted values. That points to a missed curve or interaction, which a transformation or an extra term may fix.']);
          }
          if (v.ordered) {
            let num = 0, den = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { den += (e[i] - mean) ** 2; if (i) num += (e[i] - e[i - 1]) ** 2; }
            const dw = num / den, r1 = 1 - dw / 2;
            kv.push(['Durbin–Watson (lag-1 autocorrelation)', `${HM.fmt(dw, 2)} (r₁ ≈ ${HM.fmt(r1, 2)})`]);
            if (r1 > 0.3) flags.push(['warn', `Neighbouring residuals are correlated (r₁ ≈ ${HM.fmt(r1, 2)}). The observations carry less independent information than their number suggests; see the independence check.`]);
          }
          // residual plot
          const W = 520, Hh = 210, pad = 34, xs = fit || e.map((_, i) => i + 1), x0 = Math.min(...xs), x1 = Math.max(...xs), lim = Math.max(...e.map(Math.abs)) || 1;
          const X = x => pad + (x1 > x0 ? (x - x0) / (x1 - x0) : 0.5) * (W - pad - 10), Y = y => Hh / 2 - y / lim * (Hh / 2 - 14);
          let svg = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${Hh}" style="width:100%;max-width:${W}px;height:auto;display:block;color:inherit" role="img" aria-label="Residual plot">`;
          svg += `<line x1="${pad}" x2="${W - 10}" y1="${Y(0)}" y2="${Y(0)}" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".4"/>`;
          svg += e.map((y, i) => `<circle cx="${X(xs[i]).toFixed(1)}" cy="${Y(y).toFixed(1)}" r="2.6" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="${Math.abs(z[i]) > 3 ? 0.95 : 0.5}"/>`).join('');
          svg += `<text x="${pad}" y="12" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".7">Residual</text><text x="${W - 10}" y="${Hh - 4}" font-size="11" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".7">${fit ? 'Fitted value' : 'Row order'}</text></svg>`;
          html += '<h3>Residual diagnostic</h3>' + U.kv(kv) + svg;
          html += flags.map(([lvl, t]) => U.note(t, lvl === 'warn' ? 'warn' : 'good')).join('');
          if (!flags.length) html += U.note('No marked skew, outliers, unequal spread or curvature in these residuals. This supports, but does not prove, the assumptions for this model.', 'good');
          work.push('Skewness and excess kurtosis use the population moments; Jarque–Bera = n/6 × (skew² + kurtosis²/4), compared with χ² on 2 degrees of freedom (p = e^(−JB/2)).',
            'Unequal spread is screened with the Spearman rank correlation between |residual| and the fitted value (normal approximation, z = ρ√(n − 1)). Curvature is screened by the mean residual in each third of the fitted values.',
            'Durbin–Watson = Σ(eₜ − eₜ₋₁)² ÷ Σ(eₜ − ē)², only meaningful when the rows are in time or spatial order. Values near 2 mean no lag-1 autocorrelation.',
            'These are screening statistics for one set of residuals, not a full model diagnosis. Influence (leverage, Cook’s distance) needs the predictors, which are not entered here.');
        }
      }
      return { html, work };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

::: {.ck-refs}
**Scope note**

This beta tool is a structured checklist, not a test of model assumptions. The relevant assumptions depend on the exact statistical procedure and intended inference. An unchecked item only means that you have not marked the check as reported; it does not establish that the paper omitted it. The residual diagnostic screens one set of residuals; it does not replace a full model diagnosis.

Jarque, C.M., Bera, A.K. (1987). A test for normality of observations and regression residuals. *International Statistical Review* 55, 163–172. [doi:10.2307/1403192](https://doi.org/10.2307/1403192)

Durbin, J., Watson, G.S. (1950). Testing for serial correlation in least squares regression. I. *Biometrika* 37, 409–428. [doi:10.1093/biomet/37.3-4.409](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/37.3-4.409)
:::

:::

::: {#model-comparison .ck-sec}

## Model comparison audit <span class="ck-beta">BETA</span>

Use this checklist when a paper claims that one model performs better than another. It checks comparability of the evaluation design. With paired fold scores it also tests the difference properly (cross-validation folds share training data, so a plain paired t-test is too optimistic), and with the counts of cases where two classifiers disagree it runs McNemar's test.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="modelcmp"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const S = window.CKSTAT;
  const fields = [
    ['data', 'Evaluation observations', [['same', 'Same held-out observations for all models'], ['different', 'Different observations / folds'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'different', 'If models are evaluated on different observations or folds, the metric difference can reflect the evaluation data as well as model performance. Prefer paired predictions on the same held-out cases where the comparison target allows it.'],
    ['scale', 'Response and scale', [['same', 'Same response, units and transformation'], ['different', 'Different response scale / target'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'different', 'Metrics on different response scales or targets are generally not directly comparable. Confirm the target, units, transformations and any retransformation correction.'],
    ['validation', 'Validation strategy', [['same', 'Same split or resampling strategy'], ['different', 'Different validation strategies'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'different', 'Different splits or resampling strategies can change the difficulty of the task. Re-evaluate models under a common strategy that matches the intended deployment setting.'],
    ['metric', 'Metric definition and direction', [['same', 'Same metric definition; direction understood'], ['different', 'Metrics differ or are not directly comparable'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'different', 'Confirm the exact metric formula, units, weighting, aggregation across folds and whether higher or lower is better. Similar names do not guarantee identical definitions.'],
    ['tuning', 'Tuning and preprocessing', [['nested', 'Tuning / preprocessing confined to training data'], ['leak', 'Possible test-data use or leakage'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'leak', 'Potential leakage: feature selection, scaling, imputation, target encoding and hyperparameter tuning should be learned inside training folds, not from held-out data.'],
    ['uncertainty', 'Uncertainty in the difference', [['reported', 'Uncertainty or paired differences reported'], ['none', 'Only point estimates reported'], ['unknown', 'Not clear from the paper']], 'none', 'Point estimates alone do not show whether a performance difference is stable. Consider paired differences across appropriate resamples or an independent test set, while avoiding treating dependent folds as independent replicates.']
  ];
  const ex = 'model A,model B\n0.412,0.424\n0.398,0.400\n0.445,0.455\n0.420,0.416\n0.405,0.420\n0.431,0.437\n0.415,0.426\n0.402,0.400\n0.437,0.450\n0.410,0.407';
  HM.tool({
    id: 'modelcmp', step: 'How the models were compared', units: false, hash: false,
    example: { data: 'same', scale: 'same', validation: 'same', metric: 'same', tuning: 'unknown', uncertainty: 'none', folds: ex, testfrac: 0.1, dir: 'lower', b: '', c: '' },
    inputs: [
      ...fields.map(f => ({ k: f[0], l: f[1], t: 'select', d: f[2][0][0], opts: f[2] })),
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Optional: paired scores from the same folds' },
      { k: 'folds', l: 'One line per fold (or per fold and repeat): score of model A, score of model B', t: 'textarea', rows: 6, ph: 'model A,model B\n0.41,0.43\n0.40,0.41' },
      { k: 'testfrac', l: 'Share of the data in each test fold (0.2 for 5-fold, 0.1 for 10-fold)', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'dir', l: 'For this metric', t: 'select', d: 'lower', w: 2, opts: [['lower', 'lower is better (RMSE, MAE…)'], ['higher', 'higher is better (R², accuracy…)']] },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Optional: two classifiers on the same test cases (McNemar)' },
      { k: 'b', l: 'Cases model A got right and model B got wrong', t: 'num', w: 2 },
      { k: 'c', l: 'Cases model A got wrong and model B got right', t: 'num', w: 2 }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const issues = fields.filter(f => v[f[0]] === f[3]), unknown = fields.filter(f => v[f[0]] === 'unknown');
      const level = issues.some(f => f[0] === 'tuning' || f[0] === 'scale') ? 'bad' : (issues.length || unknown.length) ? 'warn' : 'good';
      const label = level === 'bad' ? 'Potential leakage or non-comparable target' : level === 'warn' ? 'Comparability needs review' : 'Core comparability checks look aligned';
      let html = `<p><span class="tag ${level}">${label}</span></p>`;
      if (issues.length) html += '<h3>Issues to investigate</h3><ul>' + issues.map(f => `<li><strong>${f[1]}:</strong> ${f[4]}</li>`).join('') + '</ul>';
      if (unknown.length) html += '<h3>Information to locate in the paper</h3><ul>' + unknown.map(f => `<li><strong>${f[1]}:</strong> check the methods, supplement or code to confirm this choice.</li>`).join('') + '</ul>';
      if (!issues.length && !unknown.length) html += '<p>The selected answers indicate aligned evaluation conditions. This does not prove that the comparison is unbiased or that the observed difference is meaningful.</p>';
      const work = [];
      const given = x => x !== '' && x !== null && x !== undefined && isFinite(Number(x));

      // ---- paired fold scores: corrected resampled t-test ----
      const rows = S.parseRows(v.folds).filter(r => r.length >= 2);
      if (rows.length) {
        if (rows.length < 3) html += U.note('Enter scores for at least three folds.', 'warn');
        else {
          const J = rows.length, d = rows.map(r => r[0] - r[1]), dbar = d.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0) / J;
          const s2 = d.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - dbar) ** 2, 0) / (J - 1), df = J - 1;
          const mA = rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r[0], 0) / J, mB = rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r[1], 0) / J;
          const better = (v.dir === 'lower') === (dbar < 0) ? 'A' : 'B';
          const tN = s2 > 0 ? dbar / Math.sqrt(s2 / J) : Infinity, pN = s2 > 0 ? S.tTwoSided(tN, df) : 0;
          const kv = [['Folds', `${J}`], ['Mean score, model A', HM.fmt(mA, 4)], ['Mean score, model B', HM.fmt(mB, 4)], ['Mean difference (A − B)', `${HM.fmt(dbar, 4)} (model ${better} better)`], ['Model ' + better + ' wins in', `${d.filter(x => (v.dir === 'lower') === (better === 'A') ? x < 0 : x > 0).length} of ${J} folds`], ['Naive paired t-test (treats folds as independent)', `${S.fmtP(pN)}`]];
          const tf = Number(v.testfrac);
          if (given(v.testfrac) && tf > 0 && tf < 1) {
            const ratio = tf / (1 - tf), tC = s2 > 0 ? dbar / Math.sqrt((1 / J + ratio) * s2) : Infinity, pC = s2 > 0 ? S.tTwoSided(tC, df) : 0;
            kv.push(['Corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau & Bengio)', `t = ${HM.fmt(tC, 2)}, ${S.fmtP(pC)}`]);
            html += '<h3>Paired fold scores</h3>' + U.kv(kv);
            if (pN < 0.05 && pC >= 0.05) html += U.note(`The naive test calls the difference significant (${S.fmtP(pN)}), but once the overlap between training sets is accounted for it is not (${S.fmtP(pC)}). Folds share most of their training data, so their scores are not independent.`, 'bad');
            else if (pC < 0.05) html += U.note(`Model ${better} is better even after correcting for overlapping training sets (${S.fmtP(pC)}). Check that the difference is also large enough to matter in practice.`, 'good');
            else html += U.note(`No reliable difference between the models (corrected ${S.fmtP(pC)}).`, 'warn');
            work.push(`Differences d = A − B per fold; mean ${HM.fmt(dbar, 5)}, variance ${HM.fmt(s2, 6)}, J = ${J}`,
              `Corrected t = d̄ ÷ √[(1/J + n_test/n_train) × s²] = ${HM.fmt(dbar, 5)} ÷ √[(1/${J} + ${HM.fmt(ratio, 3)}) × ${HM.fmt(s2, 6)}] = ${HM.fmt(tC, 3)}, on ${df} degrees of freedom`,
              'The naive paired t-test uses s²/J and is too liberal because training sets overlap between folds (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004).');
          } else {
            html += '<h3>Paired fold scores</h3>' + U.kv(kv) + U.note('Enter the share of the data in each test fold to get the corrected test. Without it, only the naive test is shown, and it overstates significance for cross-validation.', 'warn');
          }
          if (v.data === 'different') html += U.note('You indicated the models were evaluated on different observations or folds; paired fold scores are only meaningful when both models used the same folds.', 'bad');
        }
      }

      // ---- McNemar for two classifiers ----
      if (given(v.b) || given(v.c)) {
        const b = Number(v.b), c = Number(v.c);
        if (!(given(v.b) && given(v.c)) || b < 0 || c < 0 || !Number.isInteger(b) || !Number.isInteger(c)) html += U.note('Enter both discordant counts as whole numbers.', 'warn');
        else {
          const n = b + c, pE = S.binomTwoSided(b, n), chi = n > 0 ? (Math.abs(b - c) - 1) ** 2 / n : 0;
          const better = b > c ? 'A' : b < c ? 'B' : null;
          html += '<h3>McNemar test (same test cases)</h3>' + U.kv([['Cases where the models disagree', `${n}`], ['Model A right, B wrong', `${b}`], ['Model A wrong, B right', `${c}`], ['Exact McNemar test', `${S.fmtP(pE)}`], ['χ² with continuity correction', HM.fmt(chi, 2)]]);
          html += n === 0 ? U.note('The models never disagree, so there is nothing to test.', 'warn')
            : pE < 0.05 ? U.note(`Model ${better} is more accurate on these test cases (${S.fmtP(pE)}). Cases where both models are right or both wrong do not enter the test.`, 'good')
            : U.note(`No reliable accuracy difference: the ${n} disagreements split ${b} to ${c} (${S.fmtP(pE)}).`, 'warn');
          work.push(`McNemar uses only the discordant cases: exact two-sided binomial test of ${b} against ${n} with p = 0.5 (McNemar 1947; Dietterich 1998).`);
        }
      }

      html += '<h3>Questions reviewers might ask</h3><ul><li>Were all models assessed on the same observations and target?</li><li>Were preprocessing, feature selection and tuning repeated inside each training split?</li><li>Does the validation design match the intended use (new locations, groups, or future times)?</li><li>Is the reported performance difference large relative to its uncertainty and practical importance?</li></ul>';
      work.push('Model comparisons are strongest when the evaluation target, test cases, metric definitions and resampling design are aligned. No universal threshold determines whether a model is meaningfully better.');
      return { html, work };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

::: {.ck-refs}
**Scope note**

This beta check examines the comparability of model evaluations based on your selected answers, and tests a difference only from the paired scores or counts you enter. For spatial, temporal or grouped data, validation design should reflect the intended prediction task; see Roberts et al. (2017), *Ecography*, 40, 913–929. [doi:10.1111/ecog.02881](https://doi.org/10.1111/ecog.02881).

Nadeau, C., Bengio, Y. (2003). Inference for the generalization error. *Machine Learning* 52, 239–281. [doi:10.1023/A:1024068626366](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1024068626366)

Bouckaert, R.R., Frank, E. (2004). Evaluating the replicability of significance tests for comparing learning algorithms. In: *Advances in Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (PAKDD 2004)*, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 3056, 3–12. Springer.

McNemar, Q. (1947). Note on the sampling error of the difference between correlated proportions or percentages. *Psychometrika* 12, 153–157. [doi:10.1007/BF02295996](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02295996)

Dietterich, T.G. (1998). Approximate statistical tests for comparing supervised classification learning algorithms. *Neural Computation* 10, 1895–1923. [doi:10.1162/089976698300017197](https://doi.org/10.1162/089976698300017197)
:::

:::

::: {#lab-conversions .ck-sec}

## Lab method conversions

Results from different methods aren't directly comparable. These are the common conversion factors, with the assumption behind each stated, so you can see what you're accepting when you convert.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="lc"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const CONV = {
    wb: { name: 'Walkley–Black carbon → total organic carbon', f: 1.30, fl: 'Correction factor (100 ÷ recovery %)', note: 'Walkley–Black oxidises only part of the organic carbon; 77% recovery (factor 1.30) is the classic assumption, but recovery varies from about 60% to over 90% with soil type, so a soil-specific factor is better.', from: 'WB carbon (%)', to: 'Total organic carbon (%)' },
    som: { name: 'Organic carbon → organic matter', f: 1.724, fl: 'Factor', note: '1.724 (van Bemmelen) assumes organic matter is 58% carbon. Pribyl (2010) found about 50% is closer for most soils, giving a factor of 2. Always state which factor was used.', from: 'Organic carbon (%)', to: 'Organic matter (%)' },
    loi: { name: 'Loss on ignition → organic carbon', f: 1.724, fl: 'Organic matter ÷ carbon factor', note: 'Treats all mass lost on ignition as organic matter. Clay minerals lose structural water and carbonates can decompose, so LOI overestimates organic matter in clay-rich or calcareous soils; a site-specific regression is better.', from: 'Loss on ignition (%)', to: 'Organic carbon (%)', inv: true },
    ph: { name: 'pH in water → pH in 0.01 M CaCl₂', f: 0.6, fl: 'Offset (pH units subtracted)', note: 'CaCl₂ readings are typically 0.5–0.8 lower than water readings in non-saline soils; the gap narrows in saline soils and at high pH. Use a regression from your own region where possible.', from: 'pH (water)', to: 'pH (CaCl₂)', offset: true },
    phk: { name: 'pH in water → pH in 1 M KCl', f: 0.9, fl: 'Offset (pH units subtracted)', note: 'KCl readings are usually about 0.5–1.2 lower than water; the gap varies with exchangeable acidity and is smallest in neutral to alkaline soils.', from: 'pH (water)', to: 'pH (KCl)', offset: true },
    p: { name: 'P₂O₅ → elemental P', f: 0.4364, fl: 'Factor', note: 'Exact, from molar masses (2 × 30.97 ÷ 141.94). Fertilizer labels and some labs report P₂O₅.', from: 'P₂O₅', to: 'P' },
    k: { name: 'K₂O → elemental K', f: 0.8301, fl: 'Factor', note: 'Exact, from molar masses (2 × 39.10 ÷ 94.20).', from: 'K₂O', to: 'K' },
    pct: { name: '% → g/kg', f: 10, fl: 'Factor', note: 'Exact: 1% = 10 g/kg = 10,000 mg/kg (ppm). Also, meq/100 g = cmol(+)/kg exactly.', from: '%', to: 'g/kg' }
  };
  HM.tool({
    id: 'lc', step: 'Conversion', units: false, hash: false,
    inputs: [
      { k: 'conv', l: 'Convert', t: 'select', d: 'wb', opts: Object.entries(CONV).map(([k, c]) => [k, c.name]) },
      { k: 'dir', l: 'Direction', t: 'seg', d: 'fwd', opts: [['fwd', 'Forward'], ['rev', 'Reverse']] },
      { k: 'x', l: 'Value', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'f', l: 'Factor', t: 'num', d: (u, v) => CONV[(v && v.conv) || 'wb'].f, w: 3 }
    ],
    onChange(k, api) { if (k === 'conv') api.set('f', CONV[api.get('conv')].f); },
    compute(v, U) {
      const c = CONV[v.conv], f = v.f;
      if (v.x == null || !(f > 0) && !c.offset) return U.note(`<b>Assumption:</b> ${c.note}`);
      const fwd = v.dir === 'fwd';
      let y, formula;
      if (c.offset) { y = fwd ? v.x - f : v.x + f; formula = fwd ? `${v.x} − ${f}` : `${v.x} + ${f}`; }
      else if (c.inv) { y = fwd ? v.x / f : v.x * f; formula = fwd ? `${v.x} ÷ ${f}` : `${v.x} × ${f}`; }
      else { y = fwd ? v.x * f : v.x / f; formula = fwd ? `${v.x} × ${f}` : `${v.x} ÷ ${f}`; }
      const [a, b] = fwd ? [c.from, c.to] : [c.to, c.from];
      return { html: U.big(b, HM.fmt(y, 4), `from ${a} = ${v.x}`) + U.note(`<b>Assumption:</b> ${c.note}`), work: [`${b} = ${formula} = ${HM.fmt(y, 5)}`] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**References**

Walkley, A., Black, I.A. (1934). An examination of the Degtjareff method for determining soil organic matter, and a proposed modification of the chromic acid titration method. *Soil Science* 37, 29–38.

Pribyl, D.W. (2010). A critical review of the conventional SOC to SOM conversion factor. *Geoderma* 156, 75–83. [doi:10.1016/j.geoderma.2010.02.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2010.02.003)

Ahern, C.R., Baker, D.E., Aitken, R.L. (1995). Models for relating pH measurements in water and calcium chloride for a wide range of pH, soil types and depths. *Plant and Soil* 171, 47–52. [doi:10.1007/BF00009563](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00009563)

Oxide and unit conversions are exact, from molar masses.
:::

::: {#coordinates .ck-sec}

## Coordinates and distances

A degree of longitude shrinks with latitude, so distances calculated directly on longitude and latitude are distorted, and "metres" computed from degrees are wrong. Convert a distance, or paste coordinates to check them.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="co"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const R = 6371.0088;
  HM.tool({
    id: 'co', step: 'Check', units: false, hash: false,
    inputs: [
      { k: 'mode', l: 'I want to', t: 'seg', d: 'conv', opts: [['conv', 'Convert a distance'], ['pts', 'Check coordinates']] },
      { k: 'lat', l: 'Latitude of the study area (°)', t: 'num', w: 3, show: v => v.mode === 'conv' },
      { k: 'val', l: 'Distance', t: 'num', w: 3, show: v => v.mode === 'conv' },
      { k: 'vu', l: 'Units', t: 'select', d: 'deg', show: v => v.mode === 'conv', opts: [['deg', 'degrees'], ['km', 'kilometres'], ['m', 'metres']] },
      { k: 'xy', l: 'Coordinates, one point per line: x (or longitude), y (or latitude)', t: 'textarea', rows: 5, show: v => v.mode === 'pts', ph: '-107.21, 39.40\n-107.18, 39.42' }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      if (v.mode === 'conv') {
        if (!(Math.abs(v.lat) <= 90) || !(v.val > 0) || v.lat == null) return U.empty('Enter the latitude and a distance.');
        const c = Math.cos(v.lat * Math.PI / 180), kmLat = Math.PI / 180 * R, kmLon = kmLat * c;
        if (v.vu === 'deg') return { html: U.kv([['North–south', `${HM.fmt(v.val * kmLat, 3)} km`], ['East–west', `${HM.fmt(v.val * kmLon, 3)} km`], ['East–west ÷ north–south', HM.fmt(c, 3)]]) + (c < 0.95 ? U.note(`At ${v.lat}°, a degree of longitude is only ${HM.fmt(c * 100, 0)}% of a degree of latitude. Distances or variogram ranges computed in degrees mix the two and are distorted; project the coordinates first.`) : ''), work: [`1° latitude ≈ ${HM.fmt(kmLat, 2)} km; 1° longitude ≈ ${HM.fmt(kmLat, 2)} × cos(${v.lat}°) = ${HM.fmt(kmLon, 2)} km`] };
        const km = v.vu === 'km' ? v.val : v.val / 1000;
        return { html: U.kv([['In degrees of latitude', HM.fmt(km / kmLat, 6) + '°'], ['In degrees of longitude', HM.fmt(km / kmLon, 6) + '°']]) };
      }
      const pts = String(v.xy || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.split(/[,;\t\s]+/).map(Number)).filter(q => q.length >= 2 && isFinite(q[0]) && isFinite(q[1]));
      if (pts.length < 2) return U.empty('Paste at least two points.');
      const xs = pts.map(q => q[0]), ys = pts.map(q => q[1]);
      const geo = xs.every(x => Math.abs(x) <= 180) && ys.every(y => Math.abs(y) <= 90);
      const span = Math.max(Math.max(...xs) - Math.min(...xs), Math.max(...ys) - Math.min(...ys));
      if (!geo || span > 1000) return U.note(`These look like projected coordinates (values up to ${HM.fmt(Math.max(...xs.map(Math.abs), ...ys.map(Math.abs)), 0)}), so distances can be computed directly, in the projection's units (usually metres).`, 'good') + U.note('Check the projection suits the area: UTM, or a local equal-area or conformal projection, keeps distances accurate within its zone.');
      const lat0 = ys.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / ys.length, c = Math.cos(lat0 * Math.PI / 180);
      const hav = (a, b) => { const p1 = a[1] * Math.PI / 180, p2 = b[1] * Math.PI / 180, dp = p2 - p1, dl = (b[0] - a[0]) * Math.PI / 180; return 2 * R * Math.asin(Math.sqrt(Math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + Math.cos(p1) * Math.cos(p2) * Math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2)); };
      let maxd = 0, pair = [0, 1];
      for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) for (let j = i + 1; j < pts.length; j++) { const d = hav(pts[i], pts[j]); if (d > maxd) { maxd = d; pair = [i, j]; } }
      const naive = Math.hypot(pts[pair[0]][0] - pts[pair[1]][0], pts[pair[0]][1] - pts[pair[1]][1]) * 111.195;
      return { html: U.note(`These look like longitude and latitude (around ${HM.fmt(lat0, 2)}°). Distances must be computed on the sphere or after projecting.`) +
        U.kv([['Largest true distance between points', `${HM.fmt(maxd, 3)} km`], ['Same pair if degrees are treated as flat (× 111 km)', `${HM.fmt(naive, 3)} km`], ['East–west stretch if degrees are used directly', `${HM.fmt(1 / c, 2)}×`]]) +
        (Math.abs(1 / c - 1) > 0.05 ? U.note(`Using degrees directly stretches east–west distances ${HM.fmt(1 / c, 2)}× relative to north–south here. A variogram computed this way is distorted and looks anisotropic when it isn't. Project the coordinates (for example to UTM) first.`, 'bad') : ''),
        work: ['True distance by the haversine formula with Earth radius 6,371 km', `cos(${HM.fmt(lat0, 2)}°) = ${HM.fmt(c, 3)}`] };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```


::: {.ck-refs}
**Method**

No paper needed: standard spherical geometry (haversine formula, mean Earth radius 6,371 km).
:::

:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  const secs = [...document.querySelectorAll('.ck-sec')], hub = document.getElementById('ck-hub');
  secs.forEach(sec => {
    const back = document.createElement('a'); back.className = 'ck-back'; back.href = '#'; back.textContent = '← All checks';
    sec.insertBefore(back, sec.firstChild);
    const rel = (CK.items[sec.id] || {}).rel || [];
    if (rel.length) { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.className = 'ck-rel'; d.innerHTML = `<h3>Related checks</h3><div class="cards ck-cards">${rel.map(id => CK.card(id)).join('')}</div><a class="ck-back" href="#">← All checks</a>`; sec.appendChild(d); }
  });
  function show(scroll) {
    const id = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)), target = secs.find(s => s.id === id);
    secs.forEach(s => { s.hidden = s !== target; });
    hub.hidden = !!target;
    const title = document.querySelector('#title-block-header, header.quarto-title-block');
    if (scroll) window.scrollTo({ top: 0 });
  }
  show(false);
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => show(true));
})();
</script>
```
